title: Linking: contrast, reason, purpose and result
tagline: Join ideas that disagree, explain why, say what for, or show the result — with the right linker and comma.
why: Every B1 Preliminary email and story needs to connect ideas smoothly, and examiners reward candidates who go beyond and/but/so. Although, despite, so that and as a result show you can build longer, more mature sentences — and the open cloze often tests exactly which linker fits which gap.

hook.text: Nadia: "Although it's raining, I still want to go for a run." Liam: "Because of the rain? You'll get soaked!" Nadia: "I know, so I'll take an umbrella — in order to stay a bit drier."
hook.ask: Nadia uses four different linking words: although, because of, so and in order to. Which one shows a contrast, which shows a reason, which shows a result, and which shows a purpose?

diagrams.title: Although vs despite / in spite of

rows.label: Followed by
cells: a noun or -ing form — no verb

rows.label: Example
cells: Although it was raining, we went out.

rows.label: Comma?
cells: comma after the clause if it comes first
comma after the phrase if it comes first

diagrams.title: How to punctuate a linking sentence

steps.label: Decide which idea comes first
steps.ex: Although it was raining, … / We went out although it was raining.

steps.label: Comma only when the linker starts the sentence
steps.ex: Although it was raining, we went out.

steps.label: No comma when the linker is in the middle
steps.ex: We went out although it was raining.

steps.label: however always needs its own sentence and a comma
steps.ex: It was raining. However, we went out.

head: Function
Linkers
Example
rows: although, though, even though, however, despite, in spite of
Although he was tired, he finished the race.
We stayed at home because it was cold.
so that, in order to, to
She left early in order to catch the bus.
It rained all day, so the match was cancelled.

examples.text: Although Sofia was nervous, she gave a great presentation.

examples.note: despite + noun, no verb after it

examples.text: He passed the test even though he hadn't studied much.
The film was long. However, nobody left the cinema.
examples.note: however starts a new sentence, with a comma

use.point: Reason: because, because of, as, since

examples.text: We were late because the bus didn't arrive.
The trip was cancelled because of the storm.
As it was Mateo's birthday, we brought a cake.
examples.note: as = because, often at the start of a sentence

use.point: Purpose: so that, in order to, to

examples.text: Nadia studies every evening so that she can pass her exams.
Liam left early in order to get a good seat.
examples.note: in order to + verb, a little more formal than to

examples.text: I called Sofia to ask about the homework.
examples.note: to + verb, the simplest way to say why

use.point: Result: so, therefore, as a result

examples.text: It was snowing, so school was closed.
examples.note: so joins two clauses, informal and very common

examples.text: The team trained hard. As a result, they won the final.
examples.note: as a result starts a new sentence, with a comma

examples.text: Mateo forgot his kit. Therefore, he couldn't play.

watch_out.wrong: Although it was raining, but we went out.
watch_out.right: Although it was raining, we went out.
watch_out.why: Never use although and but together — the sentence only needs one linker.

watch_out.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went out.
watch_out.why: despite/in spite of are followed by a noun or -ing, never by a full clause with a subject and verb.

watch_out.wrong: We stayed home because the cold weather.
watch_out.right: We stayed home because of the cold weather.
watch_out.why: because + clause, but because of + noun — don't mix them.

watch_out.wrong: It was late, however we kept working.
watch_out.right: It was late. However, we kept working.
watch_out.why: however needs a full stop before it, and a comma after.

watch_out.wrong: I studied hard so that pass the exam.
watch_out.right: I studied hard so that I could pass the exam.
watch_out.why: so that needs a subject and can/could/would after it.

watch_out.wrong: He is very intelligent so he doesn't study hard, however.
watch_out.right: He is very intelligent, so he doesn't study hard.
watch_out.why: Don't stack extra linkers at the end — one clear connector is enough.

l1.es: Aunque llovía, salimos, pero nos mojamos.
l1.wrong: Although it was raining, but we went out.
l1.right: Although it was raining, we went out.
l1.why: Spanish can repeat aunque…pero, but English never uses although and but in the same sentence.

l1.es: A pesar de que llovía, salimos.
l1.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went out.
l1.why: Despite/in spite of need a noun or -ing, not a full clause like a pesar de que in Spanish.

l1.es: Como era su cumpleaños, así que hicimos una fiesta.
l1.wrong: Because it was his birthday, so we had a party.
l1.right: Because it was his birthday, we had a party.
l1.why: Spanish sometimes doubles the connector (como…, así que…); English needs only one.

l1.wrong: I study for pass the exam.
l1.why: Spanish para + infinitive becomes to + verb in English, not for + verb.

remember.trick: One idea needs ONE linker — never two at once!
remember.tip: If you already used although or because, don't add but or so at the end — that's the classic double-linker mistake.

dialogue.title: The homework debate
dialogue.context: Miss Vega asks the class to debate whether homework should be banned at weekends, and Nadia, Liam, Sofia and Mateo take different sides.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Today's debate: should homework be banned at weekends? Although some of you will disagree, let's hear both sides.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Because of sport and family time, weekends should be free.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Although I understand that, students need practice, so some homework is useful.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I do extra reading at home in order to improve my English.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Despite the extra practice, most of us feel too tired to study on Sundays.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Exactly — as a result, weekend homework often isn't even finished properly.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Maybe teachers could set less homework so that we still have free time.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: A good compromise. Since you all agree on that, let's write it down.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I'll email you a summary to remind everyone of our ideas.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Great debate — however, I still hope for a homework-free Saturday!

can_do: I can show a contrast with although, though, however or despite.
I can give a reason with because, because of, as or since.
I can show a purpose with so that or in order to, and a result with so or therefore.
summary: Although/though/even though + clause; despite/in spite of + noun or -ing — never mix the two patterns.
However starts a new sentence with a comma; although joins two ideas in one sentence.
so that/in order to show purpose (why you do something); so/therefore/as a result show the result.
Never use two linkers for one idea — although…but or because…so together are always wrong.
